title: Random quantum circuits, chaos and quantum thermalization
abstract: These notes accompany lectures given in June 2025 at the summer school \emph{Fundamental Problems in Statistical Physics XVI}. They offer a short introduction to random quantum circuits as simple models for generic many-body quantum systems. They give an outline of the motivation for introducing these models, starting from ideas of random matrix theory. They also provide a sketch of calculations of some of the quantities of most physical interest, based on an average over an ensemble of systems. These quantities give insights into operator spreading, entanglement dynamics and spectral correlations.
summary: This paper introduces random quantum circuits as a powerful, universal model to study the dynamics of generic many-body quantum systems. By analyzing operator spreading, entanglement, and spectral correlations using techniques inspired by random matrix theory, it provides theoretical insights into quantum thermalization. It is highly relevant for understanding complex quantum dynamics in systems where simple analytical solutions are unavailable.
main_problem: To introduce random quantum circuits as simple, universal models for understanding generic, non-integrable many-body quantum systems.
main_result: The analysis provides insights into operator spreading, entanglement dynamics, and spectral correlations, showing that these quantities exhibit universal behavior governed by ensemble averaging.
method: The approach uses random matrix theory concepts, averaging over ensembles of unitary gates, and analyzing the evolution of operators and state vectors using tensor network formalisms.
model_or_system: The core model is the random quantum circuit (RUC) applied to a 1D chain, which serves as a proxy for generic many-body systems lacking simple quasiparticle descriptions. The analysis also considers Random Floquet Circuits (RFCs) and the Random Phase Model (RPM).
key_observables: Operator spreading (Heisenberg picture), entanglement dynamics (Schrödinger picture), and the Spectral Form Factor (SFF), K(t), which measures spectral correlations.
important_parameters: Local Hilbert space dimension (q), coupling strength ($\epsilon$), system size (L), and time/distance scales relative to coupling energies.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on ensemble averaging (over random circuits) and assumes locality in the evolution process. The results are expected to be universal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate tensor network notation for state vectors and operators, the 'brickwork' architecture of quantum circuits, and schematic diagrams detailing the evolution of operator strings and the calculation of the SFF.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the motivation by contrasting RUCs with simpler models, detailing the mathematical framework using tensor networks, and then applying this framework to calculate specific observables like operator spreading and spectral correlations.
why_interesting: This work connects fundamental concepts from random matrix theory (chaos) to concrete, physically realizable models (random circuits), providing powerful tools to study thermalization and quantum chaos in complex many-body systems relevant to AMO physics.
